title: Stage 2 actor observation and bounded buffer coalescing
purpose: Define bounded versioned actor service observations and deliver independently forceable lower-only buffer_copy_coalescing and wait-only adaptive_backpressure seams without authorizing actor scheduling, fairness, active behavior, or performance-derived selection.
scope: This specification covers behavior-neutral per-connection actor service and selected send-side and receive-side buffer-copy observations, bounded epoch aggregation, a versioned post-service Stage 1 and Stage 2 join boundary, append-only permanent raw export, explicit missing-state handling, schema and semantic validation, the safety gates required before actor_work_quantum, the legacy_current plus memory_conservative buffer_copy_coalescing seam, and the legacy_current plus one-dispatcher-turn early_delay adaptive_backpressure seam. It does not define a forceable actor policy, scalar work-unit threshold, ready-stream fairness mechanism, threshold-tuned backpressure, active_internal behavior, or production activation.
context: The shard already exposes aggregate queue-delay, service-time, wake, packet-run, and follow-on metrics, but it does not expose a versioned connection-attributable evidence contract or an exactly-once repost seam. Stage 2 must preserve the current drain loop and record honest primitives before proposing a quantum.
open_questions: Which cooperative transition and effect boundaries can yield while preserving timer priority, recovery, terminal drain, and buffer ownership?
How should complete shard observation coverage and runnable intervals be proven before cross-connection fairness statistics are accepted?

requirements.title: Record bounded behavior-neutral actor service evidence
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST support disabled and observe-only actor service instrumentation that records one versioned connection-attributable observation for each observed shard dispatch with monotonic service sequence, bounded wake identity, closed work kind, queue delay, complete service duration, connection-local inter-service gap after the first observation, exact nonnegative scheduled deadline lateness for deadline-scheduler timer work, exact posted-or-servicing connection contender count at service start when valid, exact accepted connection work items after the current dispatch when valid, pending work count, effect and follow-on counts, lifecycle disposition, explicit missing, invalid, and saturated state, and deterministic epoch aggregation; keep sink failures diagnostic-only; preserve the legacy_current shard drain, timer ordering and priority, recovery, terminal, progress, compact work-item layout, and ownership behavior; and never treat scenario, payload, requested concurrency, peer, URL, application identity, event count, pending inbox depth, queue delay, inter-service gap, service-contender count, or accepted-dispatch backlog as an invented production work-unit, runnable-connection, internal continuation-ready, oldest-item, continuous-runnable, starvation, or fairness signal.
notes: UsefulWorkUnitsUndefined remains explicit until a reviewed work-unit vector and cooperative safe checkpoints exist.
No actor_work_quantum value is forceable or active under this requirement.

requirements.title: Record bounded behavior-neutral buffer-copy evidence
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST support disabled and observe-only connection-local buffer-copy instrumentation that records versioned legacy_current copy, reuse, formatting, combination, sent-plaintext-retention, owned path-migration retransmission-clone, receive-segment insertion or capacity-reuse, and pooled protected-packet construction operations at existing ownership boundaries; carries a compact protected-owner token through recovery and hosted endpoint handoff; reports logical bytes, copied bytes, source segments, requested and retained capacity, deterministic join scope, selected and applied identity, reason, latch, lifecycle, and explicit missing or invalid state; aggregates only fixed closed counters; keeps producer and sink failures diagnostic-only; preserves byte identity, ordering, packet protection, recovery, congestion, pacing, flow control, hard bounds, ownership, and exactly-once release; and does not claim a distinct conservative implementation, terminal-release correlation for unimplemented paths, retained age, pool outstanding state, kernel-send acceptance, forcing, shadow selection, or active behavior until each is implemented and reviewed.
notes: Only legacy_current is a real buffer-copy policy value in this slice.
The observation seam cannot be used as fabricated counterfactual policy coverage.

requirements.title: Seal unified evidence at a versioned post-service boundary
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST publish an eligible adaptive-runtime epoch only after the serviced transition, effects, follow-on measurement, actor observation, and owned work-item or connection-event resource release; record a versioned bounded boundary containing the connection epoch key, exact end tick, execution source, disposition, actor-publication state, release completion, and explicit fault or missing validity; require exact monotonic connection-observation, receive-credit, boundary, Stage 1, actor, and buffer join keys before resetting any accumulator; keep mismatched, duplicate, out-of-order, failed-sink, and partial evidence explicit and behavior-neutral; and preserve legacy_current policy application, protocol progress, recovery, cancellation, disposal, terminal work, and ownership.
notes: The connection-local joined record does not invent run, host, binary, workload, checksum, or classification provenance.
Permanent raw-file export is governed separately by REQ-QUIC-CRT-0184.

requirements.title: Export append-only unified Stage 1 and Stage 2 raw evidence
requirements.statement: The permanent raw QUIC evidence host MUST configure one connection-local accumulator as the receive-credit, all four Stage 1, actor-service, and buffer-copy evidence sink for every adaptive execution; emit one versioned unified epoch under one connection key only after an exact post-service join; emit every actor dispatch as a separate versioned sample-scoped raw record; preserve retained receive-credit and Stage 1 compatibility records without relabeling; validate unique monotonic connection epoch keys, exact observation, snapshot, boundary, Stage 1, actor-summary, and buffer joins, exact source-scoped connection-key and service-sequence coverage between actor raw records and each summarized actor range, exactly four Stage 1 axis records plus one configured buffer axis record, and no more than one non-legacy applied axis per row; retain append-only source hashes, raw rows, validation counts, manifests, and export-failure records; classify any missing, duplicate, orphan, out-of-order, or failed actor export and any unified export failure as invalid_contract; and preserve legacy_current adjacent policy application and behavior-neutral evidence failure handling.
notes: Scenario, payload, requested concurrency, peer, URL, application identity, and workload provenance remain outside the production controller input contract.
The exporter is evidence infrastructure and does not authorize a Stage 2 policy value or active behavior.

requirements.title: Correlate buffer construction with authoritative terminal release
requirements.statement: Every observed buffer lifetime MUST use a compact immutable connection-local token containing only the original operation sequence, closed path, monotonic construction tick, retained capacity, and contract version; move that token with the authoritative existing owner across transfers; create a distinct token for a clone; consume a nonempty token exactly once at the existing terminal return boundary; emit a bounded release record with closed reason, released capacity, lifetime, lifecycle, and explicit missing, duplicate, mismatch, saturated, or out-of-domain validity; keep return, progress, recovery, cancellation, reset, shutdown, disposal, and ownership authoritative when evidence is disabled, rejected, or throws; and never retain object identity, add an outstanding-operation dictionary or unbounded scan, or authorize a non-legacy buffer policy before every observed owner path is verified.
notes: Receive-segment, flow-control retry request, oversized raw queue, formatted and combined application-send payload, sent-packet plaintext retention, path-migration retransmission-clone, and pooled protected-packet ownership through hosted endpoint handoff are checkpointed; platform staging and unimplemented owner paths stay explicit and non-forceable until separately checkpointed.
Ownership transfer is not terminal release and cannot create a duplicate completion outcome.

requirements.title: Define actor work vectors and exactly-once continuation repost ownership
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST preserve one actor dispatch as a versioned bounded vector of closed work kind, dispatch count, effect count, application-send follow-ons, flow-control follow-ons, stream-capacity follow-ons, service duration, and optional queue delay without collapsing unlike work into an unreviewed scalar; provide a connection-local generation-token repost primitive whose idle, posted, servicing, repost-requested, and stopped transitions coalesce concurrent requests, reject stale or duplicate tokens, create at most one enqueue owner per generation, fail closed after an abandoned post or stop, and avoid lost requests across service completion; and keep that primitive behavior-neutral and disconnected from shard scheduling until exact remaining-work signals, reviewed cooperative boundaries, timer priority, recovery, terminal drain, cancellation, disposal, and buffer ownership across yield are implemented and verified.
notes: The useful-work vector is evidence, not a scalar quantum or production controller rule.
The repost gate does not enqueue, execute, preempt, or own protocol work and is not yet connected to the legacy_current shard drain.

requirements.title: Account exactly for posted or servicing shard connections
requirements.statement: The shard MUST maintain an exact bounded count of connections with at least one accepted posted or servicing shard work item by incrementing a connection-local outstanding count before enqueue, incrementing the shard count only on the zero-to-one connection transition, carrying acceptance in compact work-item flag storage, rolling back rejected enqueue, decrementing after post-service publication and resource release or shutdown drain, decrementing the shard count only on the one-to-zero connection transition, failing closed on saturation or underflow, preserving the 144-byte work-item layout, timer provenance, resource ownership, cancellation, disposal, terminal drain, and legacy scheduling, and withholding any runnable-connection, continuous-runnable, starvation, fairness, or controller-input interpretation until a later versioned observation contract and complete-shard coverage proof are reviewed.
notes: Actor observation and epoch v4 retain the exact count at service start with missing, invalid, and saturated state; unified evidence and raw v5 plus actor raw v3 preserve exact per-epoch aggregation and raw membership while retained versions remain immutable.
MissingRunnableConnectionCount remains authoritative until a distinct runnable-state contract is implemented.

requirements.title: Record exact accepted connection work after each dispatch
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST capture before current-item accounting completion the exact connection-local count of already accepted shard work items remaining after each observed dispatch; expose null plus explicit missing, invalid, or saturated validity when the accounting state cannot support an exact value; aggregate observation coverage, total, maximum, and positive-backlog turns with saturating fixed fields; validate those aggregates against exact source-scoped raw dispatch membership; preserve the complete work-item transition, effect, handoff, resource-release, post-service, timer, recovery, terminal, cancellation, disposal, ownership, and legacy scheduling boundary; and keep the accepted-dispatch backlog distinct from runnable state, internal continuation readiness, starvation, fairness, scalar work units, repost ownership, controller input, and active policy behavior.
notes: The exact value covers already accepted connection dispatches only; it does not enumerate or claim readiness of internal protocol queues.
The continuation repost gate remains disconnected and actor_work_quantum remains legacy_current and non-forceable.

requirements.title: Record exact per-producer continuation assessment
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST record after each observed dispatch a versioned fixed-field assessment for application-send, flow-control-credit, and stream-capacity internal producers using the closed not_assessed, drained, scheduled, blocked, ready_after_cooperative_yield, and invalid states with null remaining count for not_assessed or invalid, zero for drained, and a positive bounded count for scheduled, blocked, or ready_after_cooperative_yield; mark incomplete or invalid state explicitly; aggregate complete coverage and per-producer observation, drained, scheduled, blocked, ready, and maximum-remaining counts; validate every state/count pair and aggregate against exact source-scoped raw dispatch membership; preserve existing timer, congestion, pacing, recovery, flow-control, terminal, cancellation, disposal, ownership, retry, queue-order, and legacy scheduling authority; reserve ready_after_cooperative_yield for a separately reviewed safe yield that owns exactly resumable work; and keep the assessment behavior-neutral, disconnected from the repost gate, unavailable as a controller input, and distinct from accepted backlog, pending depth, runnable state, starvation, fairness, and active policy behavior.
notes: No current runtime path emits ready_after_cooperative_yield; scheduled and blocked work remain non-runnable observations.
The generation-token repost gate remains disconnected and actor_work_quantum remains legacy_current and non-forceable.

requirements.title: Force bounded buffer coalescing without widening a legal packet plan
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST expose the buffer_copy_coalescing axis with the closed legacy_current and memory_conservative values; preserve the exact legacy combined-application-send construction for legacy_current; implement memory_conservative as a lower-only cap of two source segments after the Stage 1 planner has produced an already legal packet plan and before the combined owner is rented; support disabled, observe-only, shadow, forced-legacy, and forced-memory-conservative operation with forced, recommended, selected, and applied identities kept distinct; latch the decision through the resulting buffer lifetime; fall back to legacy_current with bounded missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, invalid, out-of-domain, lifecycle, and ownership reasons; keep Stage 1 selection, priority, same-stream order, application bytes, FIN, reset, cancellation, disposal, flow control, stream capacity, packet size, congestion, pacing, anti-amplification, recovery, packet protection, exactly-once owner transfer, and terminal release authoritative under every forced value; emit versioned operation and unified-epoch policy provenance with exact legal and applied segment counts; reject simultaneous behavior-distinct forcing of any adjacent axis; independently prove force-legacy rollback; and keep active_internal and production selection unavailable.
notes: The fixed cap of two is the smallest distinct coalesced construction and is a reviewed conservative mechanism value, not a performance-derived threshold.
The buffer policy may shorten but never widen the Stage 1 legal prefix; application_send_batch_formation remains selected and applied independently.
Measurement, threshold tuning, active_internal, and production activation remain outside this requirement.

requirements.title: Force bounded wait-only adaptive backpressure without weakening progress
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST expose the adaptive_backpressure axis with the closed legacy_current and early_delay values; preserve immediate application admission under existing authoritative hard limits for legacy_current; implement early_delay as at most one immediately posted dispatcher or actor turn before a new application admission only when an earlier admitted application-send operation remains queued; evaluate the decision once before stream reservation or owner admission and latch it for that admission only; support disabled, observe-only, shadow, forced-legacy, and forced-early-delay operation with forced, recommended, selected, and applied identities kept distinct; never reject or fail an admission as policy behavior, raise a hard limit, wait for acknowledgment, credit, peer, network, congestion, pacing, socket, or recovery progress, or change already-admitted ownership; make cancellation, disposal, terminal removal, lifecycle, invalid observation, continuation availability, hard queue, buffer, stream and flow-control limits, congestion, pacing, recovery, ownership, and exactly-once completion authoritative under every forced value; make a stale or removed posted continuation a no-op and use the existing failure completion if posting fails; record versioned sample-scoped admission observations and configured unified-epoch provenance with exact source-scoped connection and operation-sequence joins, explicit missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, invalid, and out-of-domain state, bounded reasons and safety overrides, and distinct epoch and sample counts; reject simultaneous behavior-distinct forcing of adjacent axes; independently prove force-legacy rollback; and keep active_internal and production selection unavailable.
notes: early_delay is a reviewed conservative mechanism value, not a performance-derived threshold or a promise of improvement.
The continuation is posted immediately and the policy is evaluated once, so the axis cannot wait for external progress or self-reinforce.
Measurement, threshold tuning, active_internal, and production activation remain outside this requirement.
